I pulled the usage CSV (attached) showing the burst, but our procurement team needs a clear prorated invoice and VAT handling before we can process payment.

Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-month capacity top-up charge (May) — help?

Hi Olivia — thanks for the file, that really helps. I pulled the records and did a quick look at the allocation windows. Short answers first:

- Proration basis: Redwood prorates capacity top-ups on a per-hour basis for transient seat increases that are under 14 days. In this case the 8-seat burst from 2027-05-18 02:00 UTC to 2027-05-21 12:30 UTC was charged hourly.
- Billing flow: We can either: (A) issue a standalone prorated invoice for the top-up (recommended if you need a separate VAT document), or (B) include the adjustment as an interim credit/charge on your May monthly invoice. Which do you prefer?
- VAT: If FisherLabs provides a valid EU VAT ID and requests a standalone invoice, we can apply reverse-charge on that invoice (no VAT collected). If you prefer the adjustment as part of the monthly invoice, please confirm your VAT ID so the combined invoice has the correct tax point.

I've attached a provisional calculation (PRORATE_CALC_20270520.xlsx) showing: hourly seat-rate assumptions (USD per GPU-hour), total GPU-hours for the burst, and the resulting USD subtotal and estimated conversion for your billing currency. This is a working calc — if you want I can convert to EUR with a timestamped FX rate and generate the draft invoice.

Next steps: please confirm (1) standalone invoice vs include on May invoice, (2) VAT ID to use, and (3) preferred payment terms (bank transfer / wire vs. card on file).

Best,
Kimberly Park

Hi Olivia / Kim — looping in Finance (Aditya) because there are two practical settlement routes and I want to make sure we pick the least friction option for FisherLabs.

Options we can execute quickly:
1) Issue a standalone prorated invoice (recommended if you need a separate tax document). We will mark it with the exact usage window and apply reverse-charge if we have your EU VAT ID on file. Payment via bank transfer clears the quickest for most EU customers.
2) Apply an interim adjustment as a credit/charge on your May invoice. Simpler for bookkeeping but sometimes clobbers VAT fields if the VAT ID isn't present on the account.

Technical note on the calculation in the attached: we use per-GPU-hour rates tied to your committed capacity band (per your contract DL-8742). For short bursts (<14 days) we charge based on the maximum concurrent seats in each hour, capped at your committed pool. The attached sheet breaks it down hour-by-hour and sums the prorate.

If you pick (1) we'll produce an invoice with: description "Mid-cycle capacity top-up (2027-05-18 02:00 UTC — 2027-05-21 12:30 UTC)", quantity: computed GPU-hours, unit price: USD XX.XX / GPU-hour, subtotal, and VAT section (reverse-charge if VAT ID provided). If you pick (2) we'll include narrative on the May invoice referencing the same details.

Aditya — can Finance fast-track a provisional standalone invoice if OLivia confirms the VAT ID and bank details? Also confirm whether we can apply a one-off credit if we discover any double-charge after final audit.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
